target: QD archive geometry: the 4-tuple cell (bottleneck, representation_family, selection_family, evaluation_regime)
proposal: Stop requiring all four coordinates to be known before a genome occupies a cell. Replace the single 4-tuple archive with MARGINAL and PAIRWISE archives: a paper contributes to every axis and axis-pair it can be placed on, and coverage holes are computed per axis-pair rather than per 4-tuple.

evidence_that_motivates_it.argument: Per-axis hit rates are 21-44%. A conjunction of three such axes yields roughly 0.3^3 = 2.7% jointly, which is what is observed (3.3%). Adding a second independent tagger raised marginals but only moved the joint rate to 5.7%, because the conjunction multiplies. The 4-tuple is therefore not measurable at any tagging quality realistically reachable from abstracts, and an archive that cannot be populated cannot support a coverage claim.

frozen_test_it_must_beat.protocol: Hold out 25% of abstract-bearing genomes. Build both archives on the remaining 75%. For each held-out paper ask: (a) does the archive place it at all, and (b) are its nearest archive neighbours papers sharing MECHANISM rather than merely vocabulary, judged by whether the neighbour's mechanism tags overlap on a tag the held-out paper's TITLE does not contain.
frozen_test_it_must_beat.pass_condition: the pairwise archive must place a strictly larger fraction of held-out papers AND not degrade the cross-field neighbour quality of those it already placed. Coverage gained by placing papers arbitrarily is not a pass.
frozen_test_it_must_beat.must_be_run_before: any hole is reported as a research gap in the 48h final report

explicitly_not_done: NOT APPLIED. The archive geometry is unchanged and hole proposal remains BLOCKED at the 25% classification threshold. Applying a taxonomy mutation because it would raise our own coverage number is the failure mode the mutation rules exist to prevent.

reason: the arithmetic in the original justification was imprecise and is corrected here rather than left standing; a mutation resting on a mis-stated measurement could be applied for the wrong reason
original_claim: attributed the whole 3.3% classification rate to the 3-axis conjunction

corrected_decomposition.step2_bottleneck_survives: 4/9 under the old unweighted tie rule = 3.2% overall
corrected_decomposition.note: the bottleneck tie was an INSTRUMENT defect, not a taxonomy one, and was fixed directly: ties were manufactured by the concept tagger mapping OpenAlex's generic 'Selection (genetic algorithm)' / 'Genetic algorithm' / 'Evolutionary algorithm' onto tournament_selection, which then tied against whatever specific mechanism each paper was actually about. Four canonical lexicase papers were unclassifiable while carrying the tag `lexicase`.

does_the_proposal_still_stand: YES, and on firmer ground. Even with a perfect bottleneck rule the ceiling is 7.2%, because only 9 of 125 papers get all three descriptor axes. That is far below the 25% threshold and cannot be reached by tie-breaking. The conjunction remains the binding constraint; the correction is that it accounts for 7.2%, not 3.3%.

finding: abstract coverage is strongly ERA-DEPENDENT, so the campaign's evidence is systematically thinner for older literature

measurement.note: the modern-topic lanes sit at 92-100%; the historical lane at 74%; pre-2000 papers overall at 48%

why_it_matters: P1/P2/P3 cannot run on a title, so every claim-ledger statistic is computed over a corpus that is progressively thinner backwards in time
the brief locates failure cartography and historical boundaries precisely in the older literature -- the region where our evidence is weakest

THREAT TO THE HISTORICAL BACKTEST (brief section 15): a map built from a pre-2000 cutoff will be handicapped by 48% abstract coverage against 95%+ today. If early-cutoff maps underperform, that is confounded with evidence availability and CANNOT be read as the map lacking foresight. Recorded BEFORE the backtest runs, so it cannot be invoked afterwards to explain away a result
what_would_fix_it: full-text or abstract sources with better historical coverage. The dead S2 key is directly relevant -- its tldr field would supply text for exactly these records. Crossref and arXiv abstracts for older DOIs are an untried second route

finding: OpenAlex relevance ranking is citation-weighted, so the 'awkward' lane -- built to surface negative results, replications and critiques -- was being served the most famous papers in the field for 25 cycles

evidence.also_off_domain: top relevance hits were biology (PhyloSuite, polyploidy, vertebrate conserved elements) which the domain gate rejects, so the lane wasted budget as well as missing its target
evidence.date_sort_is_not_the_fix: sort=publication_date:desc returned all-2026, all-0-citation papers -- a recency prior swapped for a popularity one

fix: awkward lane now queries with filter cited_by_count:<100. Other lanes uncapped: the historical lane legitimately wants foundational work, which is highly cited.
not_retroactive: the 39 genomes already collected under the awkward lane were sampled by popularity and are NOT a search for negative results. Any final-report statement that the campaign searched for negative results must be scoped to cycles 026 onward, or the earlier awkward-lane cycles must be re-run under the cap.
verified_by: citation_expand median 270 vs corpus 344 -- the anti-popularity rule on the expansion lane DOES work, which is how the awkward lane's inversion became visible

finding: hole kills required occupancy on 2 of the cell's 4 coordinates, so a four-axis hole could be retired by evidence about two axes
example: cell (B1_REPRESENTATION, discrete_program, scalar_fitness, coevolved_moving) was killed by 2 arXiv hits found under the formulation 'program tournament selection', which drops the evaluation axis entirely
why_it_survived_25_cycles: killing a hole is the campaign's DESIRABLE outcome and its headline positive number, so a permissive kill rule produces results that look like progress and attracts no scrutiny. The same care applied to not over-claiming holes was not applied to not over-claiming kills.
fix: _count_relevant returns (full, partial, axes_matched); only FULL-cell occupancy feeds P6. Partial occupancy is retained as information but cannot retire a cell.
retroactive: all 4 prior kills withdrawn to COVERAGE_HOLE_CANDIDATE for re-attack

proposal: add a SCOPE axis orthogonal to the existing DOMAIN axis. DOMAIN asks 'is this computational?'; SCOPE asks 'does this paper make a claim about a SEARCH MECHANISM, or does it APPLY one to a substantive domain problem?' Admit both, label them, and compute coverage over mechanism papers only.

examples: MEGA3: Integrated software for Molecular Evolutionary Genetics Analysis
A Rapid Bootstrap Algorithm for the RAxML Web Servers
The neighbor-joining method: a new method for reconstructing phylogenetic trees
Genetic algorithm approaches for the phylogenetic analysis
evidence.why_the_gate_admits_them: their concept sets carry Biology AND Computer science AND Algorithm simultaneously, so the 2-of-3 domain vote correctly returns 'computational'. The gate is not malfunctioning -- it is answering a different question than the campaign needs asked.
evidence.residual_context: 138 of 148 abstract-bearing papers (93%) remain unplaced; 52 of those carry ZERO mechanism tags, and inspecting them is what surfaced this population.

frozen_test_it_must_beat.protocol: label a held-out sample of 40 papers by hand as MECHANISM vs APPLICATION. Require the automated SCOPE classifier to agree with the hand labels at a rate materially above the base rate of the majority class, computed with a CI, on data not used to build it.
frozen_test_it_must_beat.pass_condition: agreement above base rate with the CI excluding the base rate. A classifier that beats chance only by predicting the majority class is a failure.
frozen_test_it_must_beat.must_run_before: any coverage or hole statistic is reported scoped to mechanism papers

explicitly_not_done: NOT APPLIED. No paper is reclassified and no coverage number changes. Note also that an APPLICATION paper is not worthless here -- a GA applied to phylogenetics may still report a failure mode -- so the proposal LABELS rather than excludes.
relationship_to_TX_001: independent. TX-001 concerns archive geometry (the 4-tuple conjunction); TX-002 concerns which papers should populate it. Either could pass alone.

severity: HIGH -- the coordinate system cannot represent one of the five fields the campaign was chartered to map
target: QD_AXES selection_family and evaluation_regime; descriptors_from mapping
finding: mechanistic interpretability papers are tagged BETTER than evolutionary-computation papers and placed WORSE. They are not unrecognised -- they are inexpressible.

evidence.root_cause: circuit_discovery and causal_attribution are assigned to B2_CREDIT_SEARCH in MECHANISM_BOTTLENECK but have NO entry in the descriptors_from selection map, so they return selection_family=unknown. And no evaluation_regime value describes an interpretability assay: the options are fixed_test_suite, scalar_objective, behavioral_descriptor, coevolved_moving, formal_verifier. An MI paper evaluates by faithfulness of an extracted subgraph to a reference model -- none of those.

proposal: ADD selection_family value 'causal_intervention' (credit assigned by ablating or patching a component and measuring the effect) and evaluation_regime value 'faithfulness_to_reference' (success judged by how well an extracted structure reproduces a reference computation). Map circuit_discovery, causal_attribution and distillation onto them.

frozen_test_it_must_beat.protocol: hold out the 19 MI papers. Build the archive on the rest. Insert them blind and ask whether each MI paper's nearest occupied cells contain NON-MI papers sharing a mechanism -- e.g. does circuit discovery land near sparse discrete search or program pruning, rather than only near other papers containing the word 'transformer'.
frozen_test_it_must_beat.pass_condition: a majority of held-out MI papers must have at least one cross-field neighbour that shares a mechanism tag ABSENT from the MI paper's own title. Adding axis values that place MI papers only next to other MI papers is a lexical partition wearing new coordinates, and fails.
frozen_test_it_must_beat.why_this_test: this IS the Rosetta Stone question the brief poses. Passing it is the difference between an operational map and a thesaurus.

explicitly_not_done: NOT APPLIED. No axis value added, no paper reclassified, no coverage number changed. Adding coordinates that would raise our own placement rate is exactly the move the mutation rules exist to prevent, and it must beat the frozen test first.
interim_reading: until this is resolved, ANY cross-field claim in the final report is unsupported: MI and EC currently share ZERO cells, and that is an artifact of the coordinate system rather than a finding about the fields.

severity: HIGH -- the collision lane is the campaign's primary instrument for finding cross-field connections, and it is not finding them
finding: collision queries retrieve papers from UNRELATED fields that share an ambiguous word, not papers that genuinely span two research communities

what_it_actually_returned: TrakEM2 Software for Neural Circuit Reconstruction (connectomics)
Quantum information processing with superconducting circuits (physics)
Quantum circuit optimizations for NISQ architectures (quantum computing)
Optimization of a GCaMP Calcium Indicator for Neural Activity (wet-lab imaging)
Sparse matrix test problems (numerical linear algebra)
evidence.the_one_that_crossed: Quantum circuit optimizations for NISQ architectures -- and it crossed into QUANTUM COMPUTING, not mechanistic interpretability
evidence.polysemous_collision_queries: 12 of 15 contain at least one of: circuit, sparse, novelty, diversity, descriptor, feature, selection, program

why_the_domain_gate_does_not_catch_it: quantum circuit optimization and connectomics software ARE computational. The gate asks a domain question and these pass it honestly. This is the same shape as TX-002 (scope != domain) but a distinct instance: there the leak was applications of search, here it is unrelated fields sharing a word.
consequence_for_the_final_report: the campaign CANNOT currently claim to have searched for cross-field connections. 2% cross-vocabulary yield over 42 papers means the collision lane has been sampling polysemy for 29 cycles. Combined with TX-003 (MI is inexpressible in the coordinates), NO cross-field claim of any kind is supported.
fix_direction_not_yet_applied: require a collision-lane result to contain vocabulary from BOTH target communities before it is counted as a collision find -- a post-hoc filter that measures yield without biasing retrieval. Rewriting the queries with disambiguating terms would manufacture the answer, which is the opposite failure.

escalation: polysemy is NOT confined to the collision lane. It is general across the seed vocabulary, and the LIM-002 citation cap exposed it rather than fixing it.

evidence.cycle_030_lane: awkward, first cycle under the LIM-002 citation cap
but_the_papers_are_off_target: A Theoretical Framework for Lagrangian Descriptors (dynamical systems)
Benchmarking of protein descriptor sets in proteochemometric modelling (chemoinformatics)
Robust Tactile Descriptors for Discriminating Objects (robotics sensing)
Robust phase-based texture descriptor for breast classification (medical imaging)
Reactivity descriptors for sulfur redox kinetics in lithium-sulfur (chemistry)
evidence.reading: the cap moved the lane from FAMOUS off-target papers to OBSCURE off-target papers. 'descriptor' is polysemous across chemistry, dynamical systems, computer vision and robotics, exactly as 'circuit' is across physics, quantum computing and connectomics.
evidence.note: the awkward lane -- the one chartered to find negative results, the most valuable literature for failure cartography -- has the WORST in-domain rate of any lane.

the_gate_is_partial_not_broken: of six cycle-030 papers, four landed in AMBIGUOUS_KEPT or UNKNOWN_KEPT and are correctly NOT counted as in-domain. Two passed as in-domain: tactile descriptors (robotics) and a texture descriptor for breast-cancer classification. So the gate absorbs most of the leak and reports the rest honestly -- the failure is upstream, in what the queries retrieve, not in what the gate admits.
consequence: in-domain YIELD, not corpus size, is the number that should be reported. 254 genomes at a 53-96% lane-dependent in-domain rate is a materially smaller corpus than 254.

severity: HIGH -- a reporting requirement was silently not delivered for 30 cycles
finding: every four-hour Charon report was written to charon/reports/ and NEVER COMMITTED. .gitignore line 28 ignores **/reports/, so all six reports existed only on this machine.
how_it_hid: the campaign wrote the file, printed the path, and I reported the path upward. Writing a file and delivering it are different acts, and nothing in the loop checked the second. git add on an ignored path fails SILENTLY when other paths in the same command succeed -- the commit looked clean.

evidence.precedent: 21 files under charon/reports/ ARE tracked, so force-add is the existing convention for that directory rather than a workaround

fix: git add -f for campaign reports; this is now part of the commit step.
lesson: the brief asked for reports so CHARON could audit trajectory. An artifact that never leaves the machine that produced it audits nothing, and the failure was invisible precisely because the local path existed and looked right.

finding: reading the surviving confounds found the priority lane was ~80%% false positive; the cycle-022 survey gate had caught none of them

theory_and_proof_papers: Convergence analysis of canonical genetic algorithms (Rudolph 1994) -- P4 fired on a Markov-chain THEOREM
Probabilistic Lexicase Selection -- causal claim about an NP-hardness result
application_papers: Tool Wear Prediction via Stacked Sparse Autoencoders -- the causal sentence was 'Inspired by the successful application of deep learning...', motivation rather than a result

fix: reports_an_experiment INVERTED: it now requires POSITIVE evidence of an experiment rather than excluding recognised non-experimental types. Excluding types one at a time as they are discovered is unbounded; requiring evidence is bounded and under-fires, which is the correct direction for this lane.
withdrawn: Convergence analysis of canonical genetic algorithms
surviving: Tool Wear Prediction via Multidimensional Stacked Sparse
Neural Architecture Search with Progressive Evaluation a
honest_note: the surviving confound(s) have NOT been verified as genuine confounds -- only as papers that ran an experiment. P4 remains a lexical instrument over abstracts.

finding: P4 checks that causal language and multiple treatment dimensions CO-OCCUR in one abstract. It cannot check that the causal claim is ABOUT the experiment. An abstract can carry a theoretical causal claim and an unrelated experiment, and P4 conflates them.

worked_examples.Probabilistic Lexicase Selection: the causal sentence is 'Due to its non-parametric and recursive nature, calculating the probability ... has been proven to be an NP-hard problem' -- a claim about a COMPLEXITY RESULT. The paper does also run experiments, so the corrected experiment gate correctly passes it, and P4 still fires on the wrong sentence.
worked_examples.Tool Wear Prediction via Stacked Sparse: the causal sentence is 'Inspired by the successful application of deep learning in many condition monitoring tasks' -- motivation, not a result attribution.

why_not_fixable_here: binding a causal clause to the experiment it describes requires reading the sentence in context, not matching it. Any regex that tried would either exclude legitimate result attributions or admit the same motivational sentences. Adding patterns until the current 4 look right would be fitting the instrument to the sample.
correct_reading_of_the_ledger: P4 CONFIRMED means: this abstract contains causal language, two or more treatment dimensions, no ablation language, and evidence that an experiment was run. That is a CANDIDATE FOR HUMAN READING, not a finding that a mechanism claim was confounded. The final report must describe the lane that way.
revised_lane_status: 4 CONFIRMED candidates, of which I judge by reading: 1 plausible (Neural Architecture Search with Progressive Evaluation -- compute-intensive evaluation phase, with representation, search_budget and compute all co-varying), 2 firing on non-experimental causal sentences, 1 unassessed. That is a candidate list, not a result.
supersedes: any earlier framing of the confound count as a substantive campaign output

finding: the campaign's USABLE output peaked in the first ten cycles and has declined monotonically since. Raw corpus growth has continued; placed-paper growth has stopped.
why: early cycles hit core evolutionary-computation vocabulary, which the tagger covers. Later cycles moved into mechanistic interpretability (TX-003: inexpressible in the coordinates), collision queries (LIM-004: polysemy, 2% cross-field yield) and the awkward lane (53% in-domain). The instrument covers the region the campaign started in and degrades as it moves outward -- which is the opposite of what a cartography needs.
consequence: running the remaining 64 cycles under the current instrument will add corpus and produce approximately zero additional placed papers. Corpus size is not the metric and must not be reported as progress.
recommendation: spend cycles on the FROZEN TESTS that TX-001 and TX-003 already owe, rather than on further acquisition. Those tests are required campaign work (brief sections 15-17) and they are the blocking constraint: until the archive geometry and the MI coordinates are resolved, additional papers cannot be placed regardless of how many are retrieved. Acquisition is currently the cheapest thing to do and the least useful.
not_a_stop_recommendation: the campaign is not failing. It is producing a detailed, evidenced map of why this kind of map is hard to build, which the brief explicitly admits as a valid outcome. The recommendation is to change what cycles SPEND on, not to end them.

severity: CRITICAL -- produced a false PERSISTENT_COVERAGE_HOLE, the campaign's most dangerous possible output

two_interacting_defects.1_detector_unsatisfiable: the LIM-003 full-cell kill rule was correct in isolation, but _count_relevant tagged SEARCH RESULT TITLES ONLY. Zero of 258 corpus papers have a title yielding all three axes, so no hole could ever be killed and every hole trended to PERSISTENT by default. Fixed: detection now reads abstracts (0.0% -> 3.5% satisfiable).
two_interacting_defects.2_promotion_ungated: hole PROPOSAL has been blocked below 25% classification since cycle 020; PROMOTION had no gate at all. Exactly backwards -- an absence claim is stronger than a presence claim and should be gated harder. Fixed: promotion now uses the same gate.

lesson: a correct fix (LIM-003) plus an unnoticed dependency (title-only tagging) produced a worse failure than the original defect. The fix made kills impossible, and impossible kills read as confirmed absences.
substantive_finding: CEGIS/SyGuS tag as exact_search, not scalar_fitness -- they occupy a neighbouring cell. The first non-instrumental observation this campaign has produced, and it is tentative: rep=unknown on every one of them.

target: the bottleneck coordinate in the QD cell
proposal: drop bottleneck from the cell tuple. The cell becomes (representation_family, selection_family, evaluation_regime). Bottleneck is RETAINED as a derived label on the genome for reporting, but stops being a coordinate that a paper can fail to occupy.
argument: the bottleneck is not an independent observation. assign_bottleneck() votes over MECHANISM_BOTTLENECK[m] for the SAME mechanism set that descriptors_from() reads -- it is a lossy summary of the other three axes. Requiring it as a fourth coordinate multiplies the failure rate without adding information.

evidence.prospective_example: cycle 035 retrieved 'Toward automatic program synthesis' and 'From program verification to program synthesis' with rep, sel AND eval all known -- both unplaced, both lost solely to a bottleneck tie
evidence.note: this is narrower and more testable than TX-001, which proposed replacing the whole archive geometry. TX-004 removes ONE coordinate on the grounds that it is derived. If TX-004 passes, TX-001 may become unnecessary; they should be tested in that order.

frozen_test_it_must_beat.protocol: hold out 25% of abstract-bearing genomes. Build both archives -- 4-tuple and 3-tuple -- on the remaining 75%. For held-out papers, ask (a) placement rate and (b) whether the 3-tuple archive's cells still separate papers that the 4-tuple archive separated, i.e. whether removing the coordinate MERGED cells that were meaningfully distinct.
frozen_test_it_must_beat.pass_condition: placement rate strictly higher AND no pair of papers that occupied DIFFERENT 4-tuple cells collapses into the same 3-tuple cell while having different observed failure modes. Coverage bought by merging distinct experiments is not a pass.
frozen_test_it_must_beat.why: a REMOVE mutation is the easy kind to pass by accident -- deleting a constraint always raises coverage. The test must therefore check what was LOST, not what was gained.

explicitly_not_done: NOT APPLIED. The cell is unchanged and holes remain blocked.

finding: the campaign is structurally blind to LLM-guided program search, through TWO coupled gaps -- it does not retrieve that literature, and could not tag it if it did

evidence.that_one_paper: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models (FunSearch, DeepMind, Nature) -- ZERO mechanism tags, cell (B_UNASSIGNED, unknown, unknown, unknown)
evidence.reading: 1 of 283 is implausibly low for a 2026 corpus on program synthesis and search. The seed queries were written from the PRE-LLM literature's vocabulary, so the retrieval gap and the tagging gap reinforce each other: we do not ask for this work, and we could not classify it if we found it.

proposal: (a) ADD a mechanism 'llm_guided_search' with surface forms covering large language model, LLM, foundation model, prompt-based, in-context, few-shot, and map it to selection_family -- it is a PROPOSAL mechanism (what generates candidates), not a representation. (b) ADD seed queries for LLM-guided program synthesis, evolutionary prompting, and LLM-driven discovery.
why_selection_not_representation: an LLM in FunSearch proposes candidate programs that are then scored by an external evaluator. That is a variation/proposal operator sitting where mutation sits in a GA, not a new representation -- the representation is still a program. Placing it on the representation axis would be the easy error.

frozen_test_it_must_beat.protocol: retrieve 30 LLM-guided-search papers with the new seeds, hold them out, build the archive without them, insert blind. Require (a) a majority to be PLACED, and (b) their nearest occupied cells to contain PRE-LLM papers sharing a mechanism -- e.g. FunSearch landing near evolutionary program search rather than only near other LLM papers.
frozen_test_it_must_beat.pass_condition: both. Placement alone would only prove we can tag a new word. The cross-field half is what tests whether LLM-guided search is the SAME mechanism family as evolutionary search under a new proposal operator, which is the substantive claim.
frozen_test_it_must_beat.must_run_before: any final-report statement about coverage of contemporary work

explicitly_not_done: NOT APPLIED. No vocabulary added, no seed query added. Adding seeds would also change what the campaign retrieves mid-run, which needs to be a recorded decision rather than a quiet edit.
combined_reading: with TX-003, the instrument is blind to the two most active areas of 2023-2026 work in its own subject: mechanistic interpretability and LLM-guided search.

new_evidence.source: awkward lane, capped, query 'reproducibility crisis machine learning benchmark' -- a well-targeted query for exactly the literature the campaign most needs

cycle_037_yield.genuine_methodological_critique: 2 (a third match, CrisisBench, is a false positive on 'crisis' in a dataset name)
cycle_037_yield.application_papers: 9 -- ecotoxicology, condensed matter physics, immune repertoires, Bitcoin futures, bankruptcy prediction, hydrology, porous media, federated multimodal learning, MLOps tooling

new_evidence.reading: the LIM-002 citation cap fixed the POPULARITY bias -- pre-cap this lane returned papers with 60,622 citations, post-cap it returns 63-89. The residual failure is SCOPE, not popularity. Even a precisely targeted query returns ~75% application papers, and every one of them passes the domain gate honestly because they ARE machine-learning papers.

what_this_changes: TX-002 was proposed from a phylogenetics-software population found in classification residuals. This is independent evidence from a different lane, a different query type and a different paper population, reaching the same conclusion. The proposal is unchanged; its support is now two-sourced.
what_this_does_not_change: still PROPOSED_NOT_APPLIED. The frozen test (hand-label 40 held-out papers, require agreement above the majority-class base rate with a CI excluding it) has not been run.
progress_note: the awkward lane now yields roughly 17% genuine methodological critique, up from effectively zero pre-cap when it returned the field's most-cited papers. That is real measured improvement and is recorded as such, alongside the limitation.
